issue.title: Signed Pomodoro start timing — `+N` starts later
issue.description: Inside a start's `<X>`, `-` starts earlier and `+` starts later (a lone sign is one five-minute unit), so `=fix2+` writes exactly what `=fix2 ++` writes, `@foo:bar=+3` links and starts a task 15 minutes later in one item, `x=` stays a past-only record with teaching refusals, and Obsidian `se<X>` keeps byte-for-byte parity.
issue.creation_reason: Approved epic plan plan:202611/start_timing_later_offset.md requests this work

issue.title: Signed `<X>` grammar, later clock, contracts, and link starts in bob-cli
issue.description: signed_timing: extend `<X>` from `[D][-[N]]` to `[D][±[N]]` in bob-cli. Add `later_units` to the start spec and summary, move the start later in `start_block_minute`, refuse `+0` and two signs, accept every leading-`+` form (`=+3`, `=3+2`, `=+fix`, `=3+1#deep-work`, `@foo:bar=+3`, `^foo:bar=3+`), carry the sign into fit drafts and the human parse line, teach `x=3+`/`x=+`, bump the grammar revision, extend the shared MEET vectors, and document it. Trailing `+` after a bare name stays a name byte until bare_plus.
issue.creation_reason: Epic plan plan:202611/start_timing_later_offset.md defines phase signed_timing as one work unit

issue.title: Trailing `+` after bare names is timing; `#` spells names ending in `+`
issue.description: bare_plus: a bare start name now ends at its last byte that is neither a digit nor `+`, so `=fix2+`, `=fix+3`, `=bugs+2`, and `@foo:bar=fix2+` are timing while `=bob+decks` and `=bob+2fa` are unchanged. Refuse `=c++`/`=fix++` with a three-way hint, make `=#c++` legal, teach `x=fix+`, keep timing in completion round trips, emit trailing timing in bare-name fit drafts, fix the stale `=bugs+2` docs, add the differential test, bump the grammar revision, and record decisions:start-timing-is-signed.
issue.creation_reason: Epic plan plan:202611/start_timing_later_offset.md defines phase bare_plus as one work unit

issue.title: Refuse operator-only bodies after a link start, teaching the glued spelling
issue.description: link_body: an `@route:id[#name]=<X>` item whose remaining text is only session-operator tokens (`@foo:bar= ++3`) is refused instead of creating a task titled `++3`; a single `++N` body teaches the folded spelling (`@foo:bar=+3`, `@foo:bar=fix2+`), and the `^route:id=<X> ++N` near miss teaches the same fold. Bump the grammar revision and document it.
